description:
Replace Beadwork's tmux/polling worker runtime with process-local Pi child sessions owned by `pi-minions`, and reduce `pi-beadwork-extension` to a goal/domain adapter.

This epic is the implementation graph for the living baseline (not the deleted native workflow-engine pass). Children of this epic are the work. Do not implement this epic as one patch.

## Background

Today two overlapping systems exist:

- `pi-minions` already creates real in-process `AgentSession`s and tracks them in `AgentTree`, but `spawn` awaits `Promise.allSettled()` so the parent is blocked.
- `pi-beadwork-extension` can run work without blocking the parent, but does so through tmux, a worker registry, polling (`runBoundedEpicLoop`), landing, and worktrees. That path is unusable without tmux and duplicates lifecycle.

The replacement: minions owns live orchestration mechanics; beadwork owns tickets/epics/review policy; the parent model judges and acts. Child output is unstructured evidence. Creation metadata (`role`, optional `taskType`, `description`, domain fields) selects the parent nudge. There is no child result schema, no exit/wait protocol tool, no assignment permits, no disk locks, no sagas, no `--workers` coupling to minions.

A later "native orchestration" proposal invented that extra machinery. It was deleted. Do not resurrect it.

## Over-arching goals

- Beadwork usable on machines without tmux.
- Parent stays interactive while several children run.
- One live worker registry (minions), not two.
- Shared checkout is normal; coordination is advisory.
- Parent process death may kill children. Durable truth is `bw` tickets, not a job queue.
- Quality in this repo still means lint, tests, and typecheck pass; those commands are project work for implementers/reviewers, not a beadwork-owned gate.

## Locked contracts (do not re-litigate)

- `spawn` stays foreground/blocking. `orchestrate` is non-blocking and reports later via coalesced parent packets.
- `spawn` children are not in an orchestration group and do not emit packets. They also do not get comm tools. They do get beadwork inspection tools.
- `task` is the complete child prompt. Beadwork does not wrap child sessions.
- `description` is required on `orchestrate`.
- Nudges, not schemas. Event classes: `settled | aborted | failed | parentMessage`. Abort is not failure.
- Settlement is fully idle (`agent_settled` / waitForIdle), not first `agent_end`. Idle is not ticket acceptance.
- Never inject minions packets into an active parent turn (`followUp`). Coalesce including when idle. Idle continuation is for child packets, not `/bw run`.
- `/bw run` injects a prompt (epic id/title, review policy, "refresh bw and orchestrate"). Standing appendix is policy only. Not a minions packet. Not a frozen ready-ticket dump.
- One open orchestrated group per parent session; one immutable existing cwd. Goal exit forgets that group.
- No parked children. Mail vs settle is a single winner.
- Children may load beadwork; allowlist is show/list/history/ready/blocked/status/prime. Delete delegate, worker_done, land_worker, worker_check from the package entirely.
- No beadwork fleet UI. No live AgentTree import from beadwork.
- No `--workers`, `--until`, `--maxCycles`, `--noSpawn`, `--dryRun`, poll, landing, tmux, managed worktrees.
- `print`/`json` reject `orchestrate` and `/bw run`.
- Persisted `run` after `/new` or process death is interrupted: do not auto-inject.

## Do not implement

Child report/wait tools, protocolStatus, permits, bind sagas, git locks, machine-record protocols, review-subject manifests, validation task type, beadwork-owned lint/test runner, attention latches, completion tokens, pi.events handshake, Temporal-style reducers, wrapping orchestrator.ts.

## Delivery

Phase A (minions core), B (beadwork goal adapter), C (messaging/paths), D (one-epic published cutover) are one cutover train for *publication*: do not ship tmux-free beadwork until D's epic e2e passes, and do not keep tmux as fallback after that. Implementation may land in slices. Phase B is a dev slice, not a user release.

Phase E is deferred and must not block this epic.

## Success

- Parent interactive while orchestrated children run.
- One coalesced parent turn for near-simultaneous idle settlements.
- One epic implemented and reviewed through minions without tmux.
- Child settlement does not close tickets.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run test`, `npm run typecheck` pass; cutover also `npm run build` and a TUI smoke.

comments.text: Normative proposal committed on feat/reimagine-beadwork-flow as a566739 (`docs: propose native minions orchestration`). Proposal underwent repo/API archaeology plus repeated Pi-runtime, Beadwork-durability, and hostile security/coherence audits; final post-fix review reported no remaining Critical/High blockers. Planning validation: npm run lint, npm run test (424 files / 2,127 passed / 3 skipped), and npm run typecheck all passed.

Supersedes the deleted native-orchestration proposal. Living contract is process-local minions + beadwork goal adapter + parent judgment. Do not resurrect permits, result schemas, report/wait tools, git locks, or sagas. Publication is one cutover train (A–D); E is deferred and must not block this epic.

Polish round: added inspection/halt surfaces and a dedicated scope-policy e2e. Cutover epic now waits on parentMessage and mail/settle. Removed deps that serialized spawn-compat behind orchestrate and packets behind role-frontmatter parse.

Polish round 2: locked /bw abandon; expanded unit/e2e logging on lifecycle, packets, races, fixtures, and removal greps. Inspection tools + scope-policy e2e added. Spawn-compat no longer waits on orchestrate; packets no longer wait on role-frontmatter parse.

Applied approved polish: 2.6 is model-mediated group halt (1.10 blocks 2.6). Embedded normative lists in 1.2/1.8/2.1/2.2/4.5. Locked workItemId live-duplicate, nudge trim, lexical path overlap, no rate-limit product. 4.2 owns e2e harness; 4.3 and 4.6 parallel. Deferred epic lists remaining non-V1 scope. No schemas/permits/locks/wait-tools added.
